hypothesis: A Yang--Mills mass can be represented by a positive cutoff-uniform physical-length Lyapunov exponent only for an OS-compatible cocycle on a complete centered observable core, modulo tempered representation changes.
strongest_claim_level: C2 finite and restricted theorems with C3 conditional OS handoff
first_unproved_h2_inequality: Uniform H2-P1 and H2-P2 for independently constructed physical retained-state kernels, followed by observable domination H2-P3.

nodes.claim: Physical-length liminf exponent is defined on a centered changing-representation cocycle.
Positive changing-state-space weighted inequalities compose with the exact root moment.
Multiplicative step defects preserve rate when their cumulative budget plus the log root moment is strictly smaller than the declared mass budget.
Scalar weight rescaling changes the finite exponent only by an endpoint coboundary; sublinear endpoint distortion preserves the asymptotic rate.
Strict contraction at every step can have zero physical-length exponent.
Constant contraction per geometrically growing RG level gives power-law terminal-scale decay and zero physical mass.
Non-tempered changing norms can manufacture an apparent exponent for identity transport.
Every regulated transfer may be gapped while the physical-unit gap vanishes as the cutoff is removed.
A fixed auxiliary defect ceiling does not constrain an independently chosen temporal transfer gap.
Decay on an incomplete observable core can miss a lower spectral mode.
A complete normalized nonlinear Yang--Mills retained-state or disagreement kernel is constructed without assuming a gap or clustering.
Every cocycle increment is identified with actual Euclidean physical separation.
The physical kernels satisfy uniform length-scaled weighted contraction and cumulative-error/root-moment bounds.
Connected temporal correlations of a gauge-invariant core are dominated by physical defect survival with faster-decaying approximation errors.
Iteration and observable pullback give cutoff- and volume-uniform temporal exponential decay in physical distance.
A nontrivial reflection-positive continuum theory is constructed and independently identified as pure Yang--Mills.
The decaying temporal observable core is dense in the reconstructed vacuum complement.
Uniform dense-core temporal decay transfers to a positive continuum Hamiltonian gap.
Existence and a positive mass gap are proved for every compact simple gauge group.

quantifiers_required.cutoff: uniform for all sufficiently small lattice spacings
quantifiers_required.history: uniform over every admissible positive-mass retained history
quantifiers_required.distance: all sufficiently large accumulated physical lengths
quantifiers_required.observable: a gauge-invariant core dense in the reconstructed vacuum complement
quantifiers_required.representation: all admissible charts with tempered endpoint equivalence
quantifiers_required.gauge_group: every compact simple group for the full Clay target
